Competent Linear-style execution with a sparse live call and an honest provenance chip, but Cmd-K-first density suits developers more than a rep mid-call and the look is the most interchangeable in the set.

Most polished and best on mobile, with a rep-job versus buyer-role split in the library (a real enablement distinction) and a talk-time meter, but bento is a common template and the wizard has no per-field provenance.

Best live coaching on the page: schema-checked cues citing turn and criterion, a Use-line action, cooldowns and acceptance gates on 30 scripted calls, plus Retry-from-turn-8 and an SSRF-aware wizard, though it is the least distinctive look.

The orb call room is lovely to look at, but fading controls, a 6-second cue, an unlabelled numberless halo and no named next-best-question surface mean a rep who glances away loses the coaching, so it falls short of the standard.

Best mobile live-call ergonomics and a 90-second objection drill with a Biggest-miss replay in the AI voice are real habit loops, but swipe reads as a dating app, cues do not cite their source quote, and the look is default SaaS.

top5.why: The ship-it choice: the strongest live coaching of the 25 (schema-checked cues that cite a turn and criterion, a one-tap Use line, cooldowns, measurable acceptance gates), Retry-from-turn-8 turns the debrief into deliberate practice, and the 200-persona JSON packs with an SSRF-aware wizard are the most buildable library plan. For the OpenAI fund it names the model on every stage, has a Models page, and gives contributors a Codex CLI persona prompt. Pick it if you want the lowest-risk path to a demo reviewers can actually run; the look is plain but can be elevated with tokens.

The pedagogy-first choice: a visible Blind/Guided/Coached dial lets coaching fade as a rep improves, and the debrief opens on the one moment that cost the deal with a drill on the weakest skill, which is how real sales coaches work. It is also the most cutting-edge story for a fund panel (typed AI-composed blocks, model, rubric version and token cost in every debrief footer, Realtime beside ElevenLabs). Ship MomentReplay and DrillCTA in fixed order first and keep AI composition as a flagged experiment.

The sales-org choice: the AI-versus-manager calibration chart, hatched-to-solid rubric fills and a rep-by-criterion matrix are what make a sales leader trust the grader and buy it for a team. It keeps charts off the live call, its 15 job tabs match the brief word for word, and its Draft badges honestly mark unreviewed personas. Fund fit is good (grader, tokens and latency in every debrief, AGENTS.md, Codex persona-PR review), and it is the best pick if F2 revenue from training firms and call centres matters most.

The bold-identity choice: a pre-flight, HUD and black-box replay vocabulary that nobody else owns, with gauges that rewind as you scrub and an amber Estimate lamp that makes fallback grades honest. It gives the README and demo GIF the most memorable look and still covers every basic need. Trim the HUD to fewer gauges and let managers see plain labels; the fund story (per-job model attribution, cost per flight, wizard that opens a prefilled PR) is strong.

The library-and-evidence choice: the highest persona/wizard score (200 pairs in 20 industry packs, a found-first wizard with quote chips and amber inferred fields) plus the most measurable coaching loop (one cue per turn, latency budgets, Not helpful feedback that becomes a contributor eval set). It is the most contributor-friendly and honest for the OpenAI fund (provenance chip with model and latency, cost per session, no Realtime claim until built, Geist confirmed OFL). Choose it if you want depth over spectacle and are willing to add visual personality yourself.
